statements: Section 2(5) of the National Health Service (Scotland) Act 1978 gives the Scottish Ministers a general power of direction, under which each Health Board shall act subject to, and in accordance with, such regulations as may be made and such directions as may be given.
Directions under section 2(5) may be made or given generally or to meet the circumstances of a particular area or matter.
The section 2(5) power reaches both the purposes for which a Health Board was constituted and any function otherwise conferred on the Board by or under the 1978 Act or the 2021 Act.
Section 78A allows the Scottish Ministers to direct that specified functions be performed by another body or person where a service is failing.

Section 105(6) and (7) provide that a direction may be varied or revoked by subsequent directions made in like manner, and may be given either generally or in specified cases subject to exceptions and conditions.
